metadata.legal_basis: CBER Standard Operating Procedure and Policy (internal FDA procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.

candidates.statement: H. At the time of first use (i.e., at time of distribution or sale), the applicant must submit the final content of labeling and the final printed labeling as product correspondence or in an annual report if its submission coincides with distribution. This is called the First Use Notification.
candidates.context: G. During the review of an original BLA, NDA, or ANDA, CBER assigns a descriptive Proper (Established) name. CBER may use certain nomenclature conventions (e.g., United States Adopted Names (USAN), International Nonproprietary Naming (INN)). An applicant may propose a proper name in their submission for CBER to evaluate, but CBER will assign the proper name. 1. Final content of labeling is to be submitted in SPL format.

candidates.context: 2. Final printed labeling may include electronic rendering/images (e.g., .jpeg) of the packages and containers. 2253 (see 21 CFR 601.12(f)(4) and 314.81(b)(3)(i)).

candidates.statement: 1. Promotional materials that will be disseminated within 120 days of approval must be pre-submitted and reviewed prior to the BLA’s approval.

candidates.statement: L. Any approval to revised content of labeling must be reflected in all other open submissions (i.e., applicants of open labeling supplements need to update the proposed labeling in an amendment).
candidates.context: 2. Labeling coordination is led by a Regulatory Project Manager (RPM). M. Additional labeling supplements should not be submitted while another pending labeling supplement with safety changes is under review. The RPM should make review committees for the same product/same applicant aware of pending safety information for consideration in their on-going reviews.
